transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I keep making myself throw up after I eat. Sometimes I do it in the bathroom at work, or as soon as I get home. I hate it, but it’s started to feel like the only way I can calm down.
Are you making yourself throw up because you’re afraid of gaining weight?
Yes. If the scale goes up even a little, I panic. Or if my waistband feels tight under my work apron, it feels like I’ve ruined everything and I’m going to be fat by the end of the day.
Does your weight or body shape strongly affect how you feel about yourself as a person?
Yeah. I can be doing well at the shop, but then I catch my reflection in the glass and think my stomach or hips look big, and I just feel like a failure.
Are you currently at a weight that other people have told you is too low for your height?
I’m not sure. Nobody’s told me I’m too low for my height.
Before you make yourself throw up, do you ever have times when you eat a very large amount of food in a short period?
Yes. When it happens, I can eat a whole bag of chips, pastries from the corner store, leftovers, sweet drinks—just all in one sitting. I don’t really notice how much I’ve had until it’s gone.
When those eating episodes happen, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?
Yes. Once I start, it’s like I’m telling myself to stop, but my hands just keep reaching for more food. I feel like I’m watching myself do it and I can’t make myself quit.
Are you currently at a weight that is significantly below what is expected for your height?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t been told that my weight is significantly low for my height.
What is your current height and weight?
I’m not sure of my exact height or weight right now. I haven’t checked recently.
Have you missed any menstrual periods because of low weight?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really kept track of my periods closely enough to know if any were missed because of my weight.
Have your clothes recently become much looser because of weight loss?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my clothes getting a lot looser.
Would you say you look noticeably underweight to yourself or to other people?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself looking noticeably underweight, and no one has said that to me.
Has a doctor or nurse ever told you that you are underweight?
No, I don’t recall a doctor or nurse telling me that I’m underweight.
How often do these binge-and-purge episodes happen?
For the past few months, it’s been at least a couple of times most weeks. I eat a lot more than I meant to, then try to make up for it by throwing up, fasting, or exercising.
For the past 3 months, have these binge-and-purge episodes been happening at least once a week?
Yes. For months, it’s been at least a couple of times in most weeks. I eat way more than I planned, then try to undo it by throwing up, fasting, or exercising.
